item.title: Ariake Mudflats and Mudskippers — Guide
item.description: The Ariake Sea’s enormous tidal flats, exposed for kilometres at low tide, are home to one of Japan’s most endearing creatures: the mudskipper (mutsugoro), an amphibious fish that crawls, hops and skips across the wet mud on its fins, propping itself up and even leaping to defend its territory. Found in few other places in Japan, these comical, bug-eyed fish are a beloved symbol of Saga’s Ariake coast. Along the shore you can watch them and other mudflat life — crabs, shellfish and birds — in their unique tidal habitat, sometimes from viewing spots or on guided walks and tidal-flat experiences.

item.title: Ariake Sea Seafood: Oysters and Nori — Guide
item.description: The Ariake Sea, a large, shallow inland sea enclosed by Kyushu on Saga’s southern coast, is one of Japan’s most distinctive marine environments. Famous for having the largest tidal range in Japan — the sea retreats to expose vast mudflats several kilometres wide at low tide — it is an extraordinarily rich ecosystem and a major source of seafood. Saga’s Ariake coast produces some of the country’s finest nori (dried seaweed), harvested from countless racks in the shallows, along with oysters and a range of unusual local delicacies found nowhere else, including creatures of the mudflats.
